count_optional_alignment.notes: The design artefact (section 1.3) correctly specifies count? (optional) to model both Pagination.page_response routes (emit count) and hand-built routes (definitions/search, dlq, promotions — omit count). The current api.ts reflects count?: number. Note: commit d8fa8096 introduced count: number (required), which was an intermediate incorrect state — promotions.ts was passing count: response.count where the backend emits no count field. This was corrected in commit a34305f7 (ISS-0820 batch, same session) which made count optional and reverted promotions.ts. The final state on main is correct.

test_quality_iss0821.notes: cursor-page-wire-shape.test.ts provides meaningful discrimination. TC-ISS0821-03 uses Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call rather than a truthiness check, so it catches has_more: false as well as has_more: true — any future reintroduction of has_more as a field (required or optional, truthy or falsy) would fail the test. TC-ISS0821-01 confirms the no-count variant is valid and count is undefined, which would also catch a reversion to required count. The compile-time structural typing reinforces this: a required has_more: boolean would make the literal objects in the test file fail tsc.

observations.detail: Commit d8fa8096 (this batch) introduced CursorPage<T>.count as required (count: number) and promotions.ts passing count: response.count. Since promotions backend omits count, this was a type lie in the intermediate state. Commit a34305f7 (ISS-0820 batch, same session, authored 4 minutes later) corrected both issues. The final state on main is correct. Per-commit atomicity would be preferable — the count optionality fix should have been in d8fa8096, not deferred to a sibling commit.
